newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West spot power lower still as weather warms.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West spot power lower still as weather warms.

text.p: Western U.S. spot power prices slipped further amid continued above-normal temperatures for most regions, trade sources said Wednesday.
"Loads are light and there is a lot of water," said one California trader.
Recent heavy rain in California, along with above-normal precipitation in the Northwest, has kept output of low-cost hydroelectric power high.
Thursday firm, peak electricity at the California-Oregon border (COB) was quoted at $13.00-14.00 per megawatt hour (MWh), compared with $14.00-15.00 for Wednesday.
Off-peak COB was also lower at $6.00-7.00.
Firm, peak power at Mid-Columbia (Mid-C) was down at $11.50-12.00, while off-peak was at $6.00-7.00.
Firm, peak Palo Verde (PV) electricity was lower at $14.50-15.50, while off-peak was quoted $7.00-8.00 per MWh.
Next-day firm, peak power at Four Corners was quoted at $14.00-15.50, while off-peak was at $7.50-8.50.
Second-quarter COB was quoted at $10.40-$10.60, while second-quarter PV was at 14.10-$14.30, down 10-20 cents from Tuesday.
